project_type: Offline desktop app (Mathpix-class math OCR). Two processes: Tauri v2 (Rust) + React/TS shell, and a Python 3.11 FastAPI sidecar. Monorepo with pnpm workspace.
build_system: pnpm workspace at repo root (packages: apps/*). Frontend via Vite. Rust via cargo/Tauri CLI invoked as `pnpm tauri`. Engine via pip/uv in a Python 3.11 venv. PyInstaller freezes the engine into a Tauri externalBin sidecar.
test_framework: pytest (engine), vitest (frontend), cargo test (Rust supervisor). golden-file/integration tests added in later milestones.
build_command: Frontend: `pnpm --filter desktop build`. Engine freeze: `scripts/build-engine` (PyInstaller). Tauri bundle: `pnpm --filter desktop tauri build`.
test_command: Engine: `cd engine && ruff check . && black --check . && mypy texora_engine && pytest -q`. Frontend: `pnpm --filter desktop lint && pnpm --filter desktop test -- --run`. Rust: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy && cargo test` in apps/desktop/src-tauri.
verification_instructions: After every change run the relevant lint+type+test. Use ONE-SHOT commands only — never leave `pnpm tauri dev`, `pnpm dev`, or uvicorn --reload running. For the engine, start it briefly in the background for a /healthz smoke then stop it. For the Tauri 'window opens' check, build only; do not launch a dev window in automation. Clean up temp files. OCR-affecting changes would need the benchmark smoke hook, but M1 has no OCR so that hook does not apply.
snapshot_or_generated_files: PyInstaller output `apps/desktop/src-tauri/binaries/texora-engine-<TARGET_TRIPLE>[.exe]` is generated (gitignored, produced by scripts/build-engine). Tauri bundle output under apps/desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/ is generated. pnpm-lock.yaml, Cargo.lock, and engine requirements lock are the authoritative version pins and ARE committed.
environment_constraints: Windows host, bash shell. VERIFIED on this host: node v24.14.0 present; pnpm NOT installed (enable via corepack or `npm i -g pnpm`); only Python 3.14 on PATH (engine targets 3.11 — provision a 3.11 venv, e.g. `py -3.11 -m venv` or `uv python install 3.11`); rustc/cargo NOT installed; Tauri CLI consumed via pnpm devDep @tauri-apps/cli as `pnpm tauri`. CONSEQUENCE: all cargo/clippy/tauri-build checks and the real Tauri window are UNVERIFIABLE unless the coder installs the Rust toolchain; the full CI 'artifact installs and launches' is only verifiable on real GitHub runners. Flag these as host-limited; NEVER fake success. Automation = one-shot commands only.
contribution_requirements: No placeholder/stub/fake outputs in production paths (engine is a REAL FastAPI server). Pin all dependency versions; verify every library/API against current official docs; do not invent APIs. Add a license row to docs/LICENSES.md in the SAME change that adds a dependency. Python: full type hints, mypy clean, black-formatted, ruff-clean, Pydantic v2. TS: strict mode, ESLint+Prettier, components never call fetch/invoke directly (only via the single typed engine client). Rust: cargo fmt + clippy clean; supervisor is a secure client + process manager, no business logic. Engine binds 127.0.0.1 only + bearer token on every non-health route. Small conventional-commit commits; commit locally, never push. Do NOT add Surya or PyMuPDF as deps in M1.
key_patterns: Engine adapters (later milestones) implement Protocols in recognizers/base.py & layout/base.py and are wired via pipeline.yaml; UI never depends on a specific engine. SQLite access through db/ only. Exports through export/ with golden fixtures. One typed TS engine client module in apps/desktop/src wraps all invoke/events. Tauri externalBin sidecar naming: `<name>-$TARGET_TRIPLE` (triple = host: from `rustc -Vv`), with `.exe` on Windows; the sidecar base name MUST differ from the Cargo crate name (Tauri rejects a collision) — use crate `texora-desktop` + sidecar `texora-engine`.
